siblingFile: api-data/cdm-flow-state.json — GET /p0/cdm/flow/state, the per-FILE list this endpoint is a rollup of, plus the per-file row/reset/delete endpoints added 2026-08-18. The two are designed to be consumed together (rollup drives tab status/counts; file list drives file names, duplicate detection and the per-file grid).

auth.note: Handled globally by src/proxy.js + src/app/api/_lib/proxy.js. Never add auth headers per-route.

notes: 2026-08-13: First real endpoint delivered against the ConnectorState entity proposed in docs/domain-configuration-backend-requirements.md §4.1, and the discovery shape proposed in §6.3 (`GET /connectors/{connector}/state?plant_code_id=…`). The real endpoint improves on that proposal — it is NOT per-connector; one call returns ALL connectors for the plant in `data.connectors[]`.

2026-08-17 FULLY CONFIRMED via an untruncated live response for plant Plant_1 plus the Swagger UI. All SEVEN connectors confirmed BY NAME and in this order: pnid, documents, timeseries, sap, aif, gloc, lopc (`total: 7`). This supersedes the earlier note where the last four were elided as '… 4 more' and only inferred.

2026-08-17 SEMANTICS CHANGE (breaking for any status-string consumer): `status` RE-OPENS to UPLOADED while ANY file is unprocessed. PROVEN by the Plant_1 response: the `documents` connector reads `status: "UPLOADED"` while simultaneously carrying non-null `validated_at` AND `committed_at` — it IS committed, it just has 1 pending file. So `status` alone can never answer 'has this connector ever been committed?'. Use the lifecycle timestamps (monotonic, they do not re-open) for stage questions and `status` only for 'what is it waiting on right now'. The frontend does exactly this — see deriveConnectorLifecycle in src/components/admin/connectorState.js.

2026-08-17 GOTCHA: `processed_at` can be NULL on a connector that is nonetheless committed AND has every file processed. Plant_1's `sap`: `processed_at: null`, `committed_at: "2026-07-13 09:20:48"`, `counts.processed: 23`, `files_total: 23`. So `processed_at` is NOT a reliable 'has been processed' signal on its own — treat committed as implying processed, and prefer `counts` for anything file-shaped. Same row also has `last_upload_batch_id: null` and `last_run_id: null` despite 23 files, so those two are not safe to assume present either.

2026-08-17: `unprocessed_file_count` EXCLUDES failed files — it tracks pending only. Plant_1's `documents`: files_total 11 = pending 1 + processed 3 + failed 7, and `unprocessed_file_count: 1`. Anything wanting to surface failures must read `counts.failed` / `has_failures` (true on that row) separately; they will never show up in the unprocessed count.

2026-08-17: `include_groups` confirmed in the Swagger UI as an optional `boolean (query)` described 'Also return the taxonomy rollup', default `false`. The app deliberately does not send it — the per-file detail it needs comes from flow/state instead.

Swagger operationId `listConnectorStates_p0_cdm_connectors_state_get`; the literal path shown above the operation is `/p0/cdm/connectors/state` — read directly from the Swagger UI, not decoded from the operationId (which is ambiguous about slash boundaries; see CLAUDE.md's intake protocol).

`groups[]` (only present when include_groups=true) is still only confirmed for the `pnid` connector's 1-level shape (pnid/pfd/line_list/others) from the 2026-08-13 sample. `documents` (expected 2-level: type→subtype) and `sap` (expected 2-level: pipeline_group→table) group shapes remain UNCONFIRMED. Note flow/state's per-file `category` field makes groups[] unnecessary for most UI needs — the app derives from the file list instead.

`status` enum: NOT_CONFIGURED, UPLOADED and COMMITTED are now confirmed from live samples. PROCESSED / VALIDATED / FAILED are still inferred from the same-named timestamp fields and have NOT been seen as literal status strings. Backend casing is UPPER_SNAKE; the frontend's SOURCE_STATUS constants (src/components/admin/domainSources.js) are lowercase — but no string mapping was needed in the end, since the app derives stage from timestamps + counts.

`flow` vs `flows`: `flow` is the connector's primary flow; `flows[]` is every flow it owns. ALL SEVEN confirmed live on Plant_1 — pnid→['pnid'], documents→['docs'], timeseries→['ts','ts_values'], sap→['sap'], aif→['aif'], gloc→['gloc'], lopc→['lopc']. Only `documents` (→'docs') and `timeseries` (two flows) differ from their connector name. This is the join key to flow/state's `flow` query param; the frontend map is FLOWS_BY_SOURCE_TYPE in src/components/admin/connectorState.js.

Unclear whether a `?connector=` filter query param exists to fetch a single connector's state. Swagger shows only plant_code_id + include_groups, so probably not — the endpoint always returns all seven.

2026-08-18: the per-connector endpoint GET /p0/cdm/connectors/{connector}/state is CONFIRMED and now wired — it takes the connector in the PATH (not a ?connector= query param, which does not exist), and it is the only way to get include_groups for a single connector. This resolves the old open issue about filtering. It has ALWAYS validated its connector name and 422s on an unknown one — which is why it and /flow/state used to behave in opposite ways, /flow/state having silently returned an empty list for a bad `flow` until the 2026-08-18 release made it validate too.

2026-08-18: `data.status` on the per-connector endpoint is a THIRD vocabulary — UPPERCASE connector states (NOT_CONFIGURED | UPLOADED | PROCESSING | PROCESSED | IN_REVIEW | VALIDATED | COMMITTED | FAILED), which is neither the /flow/state `lifecycle` filter nor a file row's own `status`. It is the highest-rank state across every file under the connector. IN_REVIEW and PROCESSING are newly named here; the earlier note listing the enum omitted both.

endpoints.description: Lifecycle state for every connector of a plant — one rollup per connector: status, the seven standard file counts, unprocessed-file accounting, and lifecycle timestamps. Derived server-side from flow_state, so it cannot disagree with the files it summarises.

include_groups.note: Omitted in the 2026-08-17 live call and no groups key came back — hence default false.

connectors.connector: string — 'pnid' | 'documents' | 'timeseries' confirmed; sap|aif|gloc|lopc expected (the elided '… 4 more')
connectors.flow: string — primary flow name; join key to flow/state's `flow` param
connectors.flows: string[] — every flow this connector owns, e.g. timeseries → ['ts','ts_values']
connectors.status: string — NOT_CONFIGURED | UPLOADED confirmed. RE-OPENS to UPLOADED when any file is unprocessed (see notes)
connectors.configured_at: timestamp string | null — space-separated, no T, no zone: '2026-08-14 09:19:52.063562'. NOTE: flow/state returns ISO-8601 with a T for the same kind of field — the two endpoints do NOT agree on timestamp format, so parse defensively (src/lib/time parseUTC).
connectors.groups: array | absent — only when include_groups=true; see notes for confirmed/unconfirmed shapes

endpoints.sampleResponseNote: 2026-08-17 UNTRUNCATED sample (plant Plant_1), all 7 connectors: pnid COMMITTED (6/6 processed) · documents UPLOADED but committed_at set (11 files: 1 pending, 3 processed, 7 failed, has_failures true) · timeseries COMMITTED (11/11) · sap COMMITTED with processed_at NULL and both id fields null (23/23) · aif/gloc/lopc all NOT_CONFIGURED with 0 files. No groups[] key (include_groups=false).
endpoints.verdict: INTEGRATED 2026-08-17 — this endpoint now backs the entire Data Source Integration tab strip (status badge + Processed/Unprocessed file counts for all seven connectors) and replaced six localStorage keys.
endpoints.queryHook: useConnectorsState(plantCode) in src/components/admin/_queries/useDsiQueries.js; key queryKeys.domainConfig.connector.state(plant); derivation deriveConnectorLifecycle() in src/components/admin/connectorState.js

endpoints.description: ONE connector's rollup, with an optional taxonomy breakdown for the card's sub-rows. Same fields as one entry of /connectors/state, plus `groups[]` when include_groups=true.

connector.values: pnid | documents | timeseries | sap | aif | gloc | lopc — the SEVEN connector names, NOT the eight flow names. 422 on anything else.

include_groups.note: 'Also return the taxonomy rollup.' The frontend hook defaults this to TRUE, since the whole reason to call this endpoint rather than the all-connectors one is the breakdown.

data._note: Identical to one element of /connectors/state's connectors[], plus groups[] when requested.
data.status: string — UPPERCASE connector state; a THIRD vocabulary, see notes
data.flows: string[] — which flow(s) the connector spans; timeseries returns ['ts','ts_values']

groups.label: string — display text, e.g. 'Metadata Upload'
groups.counts: the same seven-key counts object as the connector rollup
groups.file_ids: number[] — flow_uid values, joinable straight to /flow/state rows

endpoints.sampleResponseNote: 2026-08-18 sample (PLANT_2, timeseries): status COMMITTED, flows ['ts','ts_values'], counts 10/10 processed, and groups[] with TWO file_role groups — 'metadata' (label 'Metadata Upload', 8 files) and 'values' (label 'Values Upload', 2 files), each carrying its own counts and file_ids. This is the first confirmed groups[] shape for a non-pnid connector.
errors: 422 {success:false, message:'Validation failed', errors:[{field:'connector', message:"'nosuch' is not a valid connector. Use one of: pnid, documents, timeseries, sap, aif, gloc, lopc."}]}
endpoints.proxyRoute: src/app/api/domain-configuration/connectors/[connector]/state/route.js. The static `state`, `labels` and `upload` siblings take precedence over this dynamic segment, so /connectors/state still resolves to the all-connectors rollup.
endpoints.queryHook: useConnectorState(plantCode, connector, { includeGroups = true }) in useDsiQueries.js; key queryKeys.domainConfig.connector.stateOne(plant, connector, includeGroups) — includeGroups is IN the key because the flag changes the response shape, and a groups-less payload must never satisfy a caller that needs groups[].

openIssues: PROCESSED / VALIDATED / FAILED have still never been observed as literal `status` strings — only NOT_CONFIGURED, UPLOADED and COMMITTED. Not blocking: the app derives stage from timestamps + counts, not from the string.
`groups[]` shape for the documents and sap connectors remains unverified (include_groups=true has never been exercised on them). Not blocking — the app uses flow/state's per-file `category` instead.
Whether `?connector=` filtering is supported is unknown; Swagger lists only plant_code_id + include_groups.
Timestamp format disagrees with flow/state (space vs T separator); neither carries a timezone designator. Both are parsed with src/lib/time's parseUTC.

`processed_at` null on a fully-processed, committed connector (Plant_1's sap) is unexplained — possibly only set by pipeline runs, while sap was committed by a different path. Worth asking the backend, since it makes `processed_at` unusable as a standalone 'is processed' signal.

`groups[]` is now confirmed for pnid (1-level) and timeseries (file_role: metadata/values). The `documents` (expected 2-level type→subtype) and `sap` (expected 2-level pipeline_group→table) group shapes remain UNCONFIRMED — include_groups=true has never been exercised on either.
